experiments.conditions: DTMB towing basin open-water test (Jessup), uniform inflow, no cavitation; Fig. 1.3.1 of the source states Rn = 1e6 (0.7R chord Reynolds number); n = 10 rps is the workshop's calculation condition and gives Re(0.7R) = 1.0e6 at J = 0.833 with nu = 1e-6, so it is used as default (the towing-tank rps itself is not stated). No blockage (towing tank).
experiments.source: Koyama (1993), Papers of Ship Research Institute Suppl. 15 (20th ITTC Propulsor Committee panel-method workshop), Table 1.3.1 (tabulated)
experiments.uncertainty: tabulated to 3 decimals (+-0.0005 KT, +-0.00005 KQ); measurement uncertainty not published; the source eta0 column disagrees with J KT/(2 pi KQ) by up to 0.014 - eta here is recomputed

sources.citation: Koyama K. (1993). Comparative calculations of propellers by surface panel method - workshop organized by the 20th ITTC Propulsor Committee. Papers of Ship Research Institute, Supplement No. 15, Tokyo. Appendix 'Input data sent': Table 1.1.1 (geometry of DTRC 4119), Table 1.3.1 and Fig. 1.3.1 (open water, Jessup).
Jessup S.D. (1989). An experimental investigation of viscous aspects of propeller blade flow. PhD thesis, The Catholic University of America (original experiment; not obtained, ProQuest 8912977).
22nd ITTC Propulsion Committee (1999). Final report and recommendations, sect. 7 (RANS/panel workshop, Grenoble 1998, DTMB P4119: D = 304.8 mm, J = 0.833, n = 10 rps, V = 2.540 m/s).
Brockett T. (1966). Minimum pressure envelopes for modified NACA-66 sections with NACA a=0.8 camber and BuShips Type I and Type II sections. DTMB Report 1780. Tables 1 and 3 (section ordinates).

notes: Classic open benchmark: no skew, no rake, nearly constant pitch (P/D 1.105 -> 1.075), hub d/D = 0.2 (Rhub = 0.2R; the blade table starts at 0.2R). Twist = atan(P/D/(pi r/R)) of the tabulated nose-tail pitch (= the table's PITCHAN). Sections NACA 66 (TMB modified nose and tail) thickness + NACA a=0.8 mean line with the station t/c and camber f/c; polars computed with XFOIL at Re 2e5-1.5e6 (chord Re ranges 3e5 at the root to 1e6 at 0.7R). The tip chord goes to zero at r/R = 1.0 (rounded tip; the table includes 0.925-0.995R). The open-water data are towing-tank values (no tunnel blockage). Expected BEM behaviour: KT/KQ near design J = 0.833 within a few percent with a Prandtl tip loss; the hub (d/D 0.2, cylindrical in the LDV tests) is not modelled. 5 measured points only; the faired curve (source Fig. 1.3.1, J 0.4-1.2) was not digitised because the table carries the same experiment.
